data.title: Domain Policy Modification Unmonitored
data.summary:
Group Policy objects linked to privileged scopes could be modified by accounts outside the
tier of the systems they govern, and the modifications produced no alert.
data.description:
Group Policy is an execution and configuration channel that reaches every joined machine.
Write access to a GPO linked to a sensitive scope is therefore equivalent to administrative
access to everything in that scope, and it is routinely delegated more widely than that
equivalence implies.

Delegation accumulates. Rights granted for a specific task remain after the task, and
nobody re-examines who can edit which policy. The result is a quiet path from an ordinary
support account to domain-wide change.

Policy modification also bypasses the controls above: it can disable logging, add firewall
rules, create scheduled tasks and install software, all through the sanctioned mechanism.
data.recommendation:
* Audit delegation on every GPO linked to a privileged scope and remove rights not required
  by a current, named responsibility.
* Alert on GPO modification, creation and linking, and treat changes to privileged scopes as
  incidents until confirmed.
* Apply administrative tiering so accounts administering workstations cannot edit policy
  affecting servers or domain controllers.
data.short_recommendation: Audit GPO delegation and alert on modification of privileged policies.

attack_techniques.technique: T1484 — Domain or Tenant Policy Modification
